post.caption: Diamond Head is named for fake diamonds. It is the crater above Honolulu, on the island of Oahu. Its Hawaiian name, Leahi, means brow of the tuna. The ridgeline looks like a tuna's fin. Visitors from Britain saw sparkling crystals and took them for diamonds. The crystals were calcite, yet the name Diamond Head stuck. An older Hawaiian name, Kaimana Hila, means Diamond Hill. The crater is a tuff cone, built in one explosive eruption. In the early 1900s, the Army used the crater as a lookout. The summit stands 232 meters above the sea.
